long_biography.plain_text:
Raised in a middle-income Wisconsin family, Smith worked newspaper and cafeteria jobs while using scholarships to attend Princeton. After Columbia Law School, he clerked for a federal judge and joined Covington & Burling, where an early interest in personal computers led him into software law. Microsoft recruited him in 1993 to head European legal and corporate affairs.

As general counsel, Smith steered settlements that moved the company beyond its antitrust battles. Promoted first to president and later to vice chair, he became a prominent voice on the public obligations of major technology companies. Beyond Microsoft, he co-founded Kids in Need of Defense to support unaccompanied children and, with his wife Kathy Surace-Smith, endowed scholarships and a human-rights clinic at Columbia.
